messages.subject: bootstrapping with covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hi list,
I currently have a sampling design where I will need to bootstrap the data
to get the sampling variance.  I have selected among several covariates for
each species of interest to find the "best" model according to AICc.  I am
using the selected covariate in the detection function for each
bootstrapped data set.  Occasionally, the bootstrapping program will select
a combination of data that does not provide enough detections for a
particular level of the covariate.  when this happens the program produces
a bunch of zeros.  My question is, is it better to ignore the zeros and
just use the data sets that produced results, (this introduces some bias
because for certain combinations of the data I don't get results), or is it
better to use a different covariate which does not produce the "best" model
but where I won't have this problem. (I could combine levels of the best
covariate, but then it's not the best covariate anymore.) I'm guessing
there is no right answer, but I'm interested in what other people might do
in this situation.

Thanks,
Robin Russell
reru...@fs.fed.us

--
